textes.Bienvenue dans les coulisses de l’aéropo: Welcome behind the scenes at Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport. Flights, passengers, airlines, aircraft and bags: its database follows the flights of its six partner airlines, in Paris and all over Europe. You help its team: Gilles at the operations center, Rachid in baggage, Odile in sales, Sabrina in customer service… Explore the database to solve the missions.
textes.Une ligne par passager inscrit, qu’il ai: One row per registered passenger, whether or not they booked a flight: first name, last name, nationality, date of birth and email address.
textes.Une ligne par compagnie aérienne : son n: One row per airline: its name, its country and its 3-letter code, used at the start of its flight numbers.
textes.Une ligne par avion : son modèle, son im: One row per aircraft: its model, its registration, its number of seats and the airline it belongs to.
textes.Une ligne par aéroport : son nom, sa vil: One row per airport: its name, its city, its country and its IATA code. Each flight links two airports (departure and arrival); an airport can have no flights.
textes.Une ligne par vol, du 10 au 13 juin 2025: One row per flight, from June 10 to 13, 2025: its airline, its aircraft, its departure and arrival airports, its date, its scheduled times and its status.
textes.Une ligne par billet : un passager sur u: One row per ticket: a passenger on a flight, with its class, its seat, its price and its purchase date. A passenger can have several tickets, sometimes on the same flight; a flight can have none.
textes.Une ligne par bagage, rattaché à un bill: One row per bag, linked to a ticket (a booking): its weight and its status. A booking can have no bags.
textes.Adresse e-mail, unique pour chaque passa: Email address, unique for each passenger (e.g. “camille.moreau@mail.fr”).
textes.Pays de la compagnie : « Allemagne », «: Country of the airline: “France”, “Germany”, “Italy”, “Portugal”, “Spain” or “United Kingdom”.
textes.Code unique de 3 lettres, repris au débu: Unique 3-letter code, used at the start of the airline’s flight numbers (e.g. “ALX” for AlphaJet).
textes.Modèle de l’avion, nom du constructeur e: Model of the aircraft, manufacturer’s name first (e.g. “Airbus A320”, “Boeing 737-800”, “Embraer E190”).
Total number of seats on the aircraft.
textes.La compagnie à laquelle appartient l’avi: The airline the aircraft belongs to.
textes.Nom complet de l’aéroport (ex. « Aéropor: Full name of the airport (e.g. “Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport”).
textes.Ville de l’aéroport (ex. « Paris », « Ne: City of the airport (e.g. “Paris”, “New York”); each city has only one airport in the database.
textes.Pays de l’aéroport, en français (ex. « E: Country of the airport, in English (e.g. “Spain”, “United Kingdom”, “United States”).
textes.Code IATA de l’aéroport, 3 lettres, uniq: IATA code of the airport, 3 letters, unique (e.g. “CDG”, “JFK”).
textes.Numéro commercial du vol, unique : le co: Flight number, unique: the airline’s code followed by 3 digits (e.g. “ALX100”).
The airline that operates the flight.
textes.L’avion affecté au vol, pris dans la flo: The aircraft assigned to the flight, taken from the same airline’s fleet.
textes.Heure de départ prévue, au format HH:MM: Scheduled departure time, in HH:MM format (e.g. “08:00”).
Scheduled arrival time, in HH:MM format.
textes.Identifiant unique de la réservation (du: Unique ID of the booking (the ticket).
The passenger who holds the ticket.
textes.Siège attribué : numéro de rang puis let: Seat assigned: row number then letter (e.g. “12A”, “2C”). A seat can only be sold once per flight.
textes.Date d’achat du billet, au format AAAA-M: Purchase date of the ticket, in YYYY-MM-DD format, always before the flight date.
textes.La réservation (le billet) à laquelle le: The booking (the ticket) the bag is linked to.
textes.Poids du bagage en kilogrammes, à une dé: Weight of the bag in kilograms, with one decimal place at most; empty (NULL) for a “Carry-on” bag, not weighed.
textes.Statut du bagage : « Enregistré », « Liv: Status of the bag: “Checked in”, “Delivered”, “Delayed”, “Lost” or “Carry-on” (kept by the passenger).
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, from June 10 to 13, 2025 (between Paris, Europe and a few cities farther away). Each flight has a status that says where it stands: scheduled, on time, delayed, cancelled or landed. Gilles runs the operations center, which follows these flights live. This morning, he has to get the travelers whose flight is delayed warned: he wants to know which flights are affected, and on what day and at what time they were supposed to leave.
textes.par date de départ, puis par heure de dé: by departure date, then by departure time, then by flight number
textes.Un seul critère suffit : le statut du vo: A single criterion is enough: the flight’s status, compared exactly with the text “Delayed”, with its capital letter. The rest is the order asked for.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website, even before booking a ticket. When signing up, each one gives their nationality (“French”, “Italian”…) and their email address. Sabrina, who runs customer service, is preparing a message just for passengers of French nationality. She wants to know who to send it to, and to which email address.
textes.La nationalité est écrite au féminin : c: Compare the nationality exactly with the text “French”. The passengers are all in the same list, there’s nothing to link.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines. Each flight links a departure airport to an arrival airport; the country and the city of each airport are stored separately, with the list of airports. Odile, the sales director, is preparing a campaign with the Spanish tourist office. She wants the list of all the flights that arrive in Spain, whatever their status, with their arrival airport and city.
textes.le nom de son aéroport d’arrivée: the name of its arrival airport
textes.les vols dont l’aéroport d’arrivée est d: the flights whose arrival airport is in the country “Spain”, whatever their status
textes.par ville d’arrivée, puis par numéro de: by arrival city, then by flight number
textes.Le vol ne connaît ses aéroports que par: The flight only knows its airports by their IDs. Link each flight to its arrival airport, not its departure one, then keep only those whose country is Spain.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells tickets on the flights of six partner airlines. Each ticket puts a passenger on a flight, in a class (Economy, Premium or Business), at a given price; the flight number is stored with the flights. In sales, Odile wants to understand where the biggest sales come from. She wants to look at the 10 tickets sold at the highest price, all airlines combined, with their class and their flight number.
textes.le numéro du vol réservé: the number of the flight booked
textes.par prix, du plus élevé au plus bas, pui: by price, highest first, then by booking ID
textes.Relie chaque billet à son vol pour obten: Link each ticket to its flight to get the number. Then sort the tickets from most to least expensive, and keep only the first ten.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle enreg: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport records each bag with its owner’s ticket, and each ticket links a passenger to a flight. A bag’s status says where it stands: checked in, carry-on, delivered, delayed or lost. Rachid runs the baggage service, in charge of finding missing suitcases. He opens a file for each lost bag: he wants to know who it belongs to and which flight it was checked in on.
textes.le prénom du passager à qui il appartien: the first name of the passenger it belongs to
textes.le numéro du vol sur lequel il voyage: the number of the flight it travels on
textes.Le bagage mène au billet, et le billet m: The bag leads to the ticket, and the ticket leads to both the passenger and the flight: you have to follow that whole path. Several lists have a status column: make it clear that you’re filtering the bag’s.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, leaving from Paris and other European cities. Each flight has a scheduled departure time and a status that says where it stands; the city of each airport is stored with the list of airports. Margaux, the station manager, organizes check-in and boarding for the flights leaving Paris. She wants to know what time each of them leaves and where it stands, whatever its status.
textes.les vols dont l’aéroport de départ est d: the flights whose departure airport is in the city “Paris”, whatever their status
textes.par heure de départ, tous jours confondu: by departure time, all days combined, then by flight number
textes.Relie chaque vol à son aéroport de dépar: Link each flight to its departure airport, not its arrival one, and keep only those in the city of Paris. The sort is on the time alone, all days combined.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website without having booked a ticket yet. The tickets are stored separately, each with the passenger it belongs to. Yannick runs the loyalty club, open to everyone who signed up. He wants to follow up with those who have never booked yet: he’ll email them a welcome offer for their first trip.
textes.les passagers qui n’ont aucune réservati: the passengers who have no booking
textes.Pars de tous les passagers et cherche le: Start from every passenger and look for their tickets. Also keep those for whom nothing is found, then keep only those: they’re the people signed up without a booking.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, from June 10 to 13, 2025. The tickets sold are stored separately, each with the flight booked; some flights have none. Gilles, who runs the operations center, wants to review these flights without a single ticket sold, even those already cancelled. He wants to know when they leave and where they stand, before talking to the airlines about them.
textes.les vols qui n’ont aucune réservation, y: the flights that have no booking, including cancelled flights
textes.par date de départ, puis par numéro de v: by departure date, then by flight number
textes.Pars de tous les vols et cherche les bil: Start from every flight and look for each one’s tickets. Also keep the flights for which no ticket is found, then keep only those.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle pèse: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport weighs each bag at the check-in desk and records its weight with the ticket it belongs to. When the weight wasn’t recorded, the cell stays empty. Thierry, in quality control, hunts down data entry slip-ups. He wants to spot every bag whose weight is missing, with its status and its booking, to check each case one by one.
textes.les bagages dont le poids n’est pas rens: the bags whose weight isn’t filled in: an empty cell (NULL)
textes.Un poids manquant n’est pas un zéro : c’: A missing weight isn’t a zero: it’s an empty cell, with no value at all. You can’t spot it with an equals sign; there’s a separate way to ask whether a cell is empty.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells tickets in three classes: Economy, Premium or Business. Each ticket links a passenger to a flight, and the same passenger can have several tickets, sometimes on the same flight. Odile, the sales director, wants to thank Business class travelers with a little note left at their seat, on board. She needs a single note per passenger and per flight booked in that class.
textes.une seule ligne par passager et par vol: a single row per passenger and per flight
textes.par nom, puis par prénom, puis par numér: by last name, then by first name, then by flight number
textes.Pars des billets de la classe Affaires e: Start from the Business class tickets and fetch the passenger’s name and the flight number. A passenger can have two Business tickets on the same flight: they must appear only once per flight.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the aircraft of six partner airlines. Each aircraft has its model (Airbus, Boeing, Embraer…), its registration and its number of seats. Gilles, who runs the operations center, wants to spot the biggest ones, those with more than 200 seats: they need more ground staff for boarding, bags and cleaning.
textes.les avions de plus de 200 sièges: the aircraft with more than 200 seats
textes.par nombre de sièges, du plus grand au p: by number of seats, largest first, then by registration
textes.Le nombre de sièges est une information: The number of seats is information about the aircraft: compare it with 200, strictly above. The aircraft are all in the same list.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle deman: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport asks every passenger who signs up on its website for an email address. It often ends with their country’s domain: “.fr” for France, “.de” for Germany… Sabrina, who runs customer service, got error messages for emails sent to Germany. She wants to check one by one the addresses that end with “.de”.
textes.les passagers dont l’adresse e-mail se t: the passengers whose email address ends with “.de”
textes.Il ne s’agit pas d’une adresse précise m: It’s not a specific address but a pattern: any start, then “.de” at the very end. Nothing must follow, otherwise other addresses slip into the result.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, from June 10 to 13, 2025. Each flight has a departure date, written year-month-day (“2025-06-10”), a scheduled departure time and a status. Gilles, who runs the operations center, is preparing the June 13 schedule. He wants to assign the ground crews based on the departure time and status of each flight planned that day, even cancelled ones.
textes.les vols dont la date de départ est le 1: the flights whose departure date is June 13, 2025, including cancelled flights
textes.par heure de départ, puis par numéro de: by departure time, then by flight number
textes.Les dates sont écrites au format AAAA-MM: Dates are written in YYYY-MM-DD format, for example “2025-06-10”.
textes.Une seule condition sur la date de dépar: A single condition on the departure date: write it exactly as in the database, year-month-day.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website, and each one gives their nationality. Many passengers share the same one: so the list of people signed up often repeats the same nationalities. Lina runs the terminal’s information desks. She’s going to order new welcome signs: to choose their languages, she wants to know which nationalities are found among the people signed up, each one only once.
textes.Il ne s’agit pas de lister les passagers: It’s not about listing the passengers but their nationalities: each one must appear only once, even if it comes up for several passengers.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells tickets in three classes: Economy, Premium or Business. The same passenger can have several tickets, and each one counts. Édouard, the airport director, checks his dashboard every morning. He wants a single figure at the top: the number of tickets sold in Business class on the partner airlines’ flights.
textes.Chaque réservation compte pour un billet: Each booking counts as one ticket, even when a passenger has several.
textes.Ne garde que les billets de la classe Af: Keep only the Business class tickets, then count them. The result is a single number.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle pèse: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport weighs each bag at the check-in desk, but the weight of a few wasn’t recorded: their cell is empty. Rachid, who runs the baggage service, is going to replace the belts and carts in the hold. Before choosing the model, he wants to know how much the heaviest suitcase weighs, among those whose weight is known.
textes.les bagages dont le poids est renseigné: the bags whose weight is filled in
textes.seulement le plus lourd : la première li: only the heaviest: the first row of the sort
textes.par poids, du plus lourd au plus léger,: by weight, heaviest first, then by bag ID
textes.Écarte d’abord les bagages sans poids. R: First leave out the bags without a weight. Then sort the others from heaviest to lightest, and keep only the first.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website; each one gives their date of birth, written year-month-day (“1984-07-12”). Coralie, in marketing, is launching an offer for more comfortable trips for passengers born before 1985. She wants their list, with their date of birth, to personalize her invitation.
textes.par date de naissance, du plus âgé au pl: by date of birth, oldest first, then by last name, then by first name
textes.Les dates de naissance sont écrites au f: Dates of birth are written in YYYY-MM-DD format.
textes.Écrites année-mois-jour, les dates se co: Written year-month-day, dates compare like text. Just compare the date of birth with January 1, 1985 written the same way: strictly before.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle tient: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport keeps a list of airports, in Europe and farther away, with for each one its name, its city, its country and its 3-letter code. A partner travel agency is preparing a tour between Spain and Portugal. Odile, the sales director, wants to send it the airports of those two countries found in this list, with their city.
textes.les aéroports du pays « Espagne » ou « P: the airports in the country “Spain” or “Portugal”
textes.par ville, puis par nom de l’aéroport: by city, then by airport name
textes.Un aéroport doit être en Espagne ou au P: An airport must be in Spain or Portugal: there are two accepted countries. You can write them as a short list of allowed values, or as two conditions of which only one has to be true.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines, from all over Europe. Each has a country and a 3-letter code, used at the start of its flight numbers. Édouard, the airport director, is going to renegotiate their contracts. He starts with the foreign airlines, the ones that aren’t French, and wants each one’s country and code.
textes.Il faut garder toutes les compagnies sau: You need to keep every airline except one kind: those whose country is France. A “not equal to” condition does the job.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, from June 10 to 13, 2025. Each flight has a scheduled departure time, written as hours and minutes with a leading zero (“07:30”). Gilles, who runs the operations center, is adding staff to the early morning crews. He wants the list of flights leaving before 9 a.m., day by day, from Paris as well as from the other airports; a departure at 9 a.m. sharp isn’t included.
textes.les vols qui partent strictement avant «: the flights leaving strictly before “09:00” (a departure at 09:00 sharp is left out)
textes.Écrites avec leurs deux chiffres, les he: Written with their two digits, times compare like text. Compare the departure time with 09:00 written the same way: strictly before.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells its tickets in three travel classes: Economy, Premium or Business. The price of each ticket is recorded, and it varies from one flight and passenger to another. Odile, the sales director, is comparing the price level of the three classes. She wants the average ticket price in each class, to check that the gap between them stays consistent.
textes.la classe du billet (une ligne par class: the ticket class (one row per class)
textes.le prix moyen de ses billets, en euros,: the average price of its tickets, in euros, rounded to two decimal places
textes.par prix moyen, du plus élevé au plus ba: by average price, highest first, then by class
textes.Il faut une ligne par classe : rassemble: You need one row per class: group the tickets of each class, calculate the average of their prices, then round it to two decimal places.
textes.D’où viennent nos passagers ?: Where do our passengers come from?
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website, and each one gives their nationality. The people signed up come from many countries, and some nationalities come up much more often than others. Lina runs the terminal’s information desks. To know which languages to train her agents in first, she wants to count the registered passengers of each nationality.
textes.le nombre de passagers inscrits de cette: the number of registered passengers of that nationality
textes.par nombre de passagers, du plus grand a: by number of passengers, largest first, then by nationality
textes.Il faut une ligne par nationalité : rass: You need one row per nationality: group the passengers who share the same one, then count how many each group contains.
textes.Le poids total des bagages: The total weight of the bags
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle enreg: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport records each bag with its weight in kilograms. Carry-on bags aren’t weighed: their weight stays empty. Rachid, who runs the baggage service, is planning the belts and the crews in the hold. He follows the workload with a single figure: the total weight of all the bags, whatever their status.
textes.le poids total des bagages : la somme de: the total weight of the bags: the sum of their weights, in kilograms, not rounded
textes.Additionne les poids de tous les bagages: Add up the weights of all the bags: the result is a single number. Empty weights are simply ignored by the sum, there’s nothing to filter.
textes.Combien de passagers ont déjà réservé ?: How many passengers have already booked?
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website without booking right away. The tickets are stored separately, each with the passenger it belongs to, and the same passenger can have several. Yannick runs the loyalty club. To measure the effect of his welcome campaigns, he wants to know how many registered travelers have already bought at least one ticket.
textes.le nombre de passagers différents qui on: the number of different passengers who have at least one booking
textes.toutes les réservations, que le vol ait: every booking, whether or not the flight has already taken place
textes.Un passager qui a plusieurs billets ne c: A passenger with several tickets only counts once.
textes.Les billets disent déjà qui a réservé. M: The tickets already say who booked. But a passenger with several tickets appears several times: count the different passengers, not the tickets.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, and each flight has a status: scheduled, on time, delayed, cancelled or landed. After a disrupted week, Sabrina, who runs customer service, has to warn the travelers affected and offer them a solution. She starts with the list of delayed or cancelled flights, with their date and status.
textes.les vols au statut « Retardé » ou « Annu: the flights with the status “Delayed” or “Cancelled”
textes.Un vol est gardé s’il est retardé ou s’i: A flight is kept if it’s delayed or if it’s cancelled: two conditions, of which only one has to be true. Write each status exactly, with its capital letter.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the aircraft of six partner airlines. Each aircraft’s model starts with its manufacturer’s name (Airbus, Boeing or Embraer), like “Airbus A320” or “Boeing 737-800”, and its registration is the number painted on its fuselage. Hervé runs the maintenance workshop. He’s welcoming technicians who specialize in the other manufacturers and don’t work on Airbus aircraft: to prepare their schedule, he wants the list of aircraft that aren’t Airbus.
textes.les avions dont le modèle ne commence pa: the aircraft whose model doesn’t start with “Airbus”
textes.Il faut écarter tous les modèles qui com: You need to leave out every model that starts with “Airbus”, whatever follows. Look for a pattern, then keep what doesn’t match it.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website; each one gives their first name, last name and nationality. Lina, who runs the arrivals welcome desk, is expecting a group of Japanese travelers. She wants to print a welcome sign with each one’s name, the first name then the last name in a single column, separated by a space, to hold up at the arrivals exit.
textes.le prénom et le nom du passager dans une: the passenger’s first name and last name in a single column, separated by a space (for example “Camille Moreau”)
textes.Il faut fabriquer un seul texte à partir: You need to make a single text out of two: the first name, a space, then the last name, stuck together end to end. The sort, though, is on the last name alone, not on that combined text.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website; each one gives their date of birth, written year-month-day. Every year, Coralie, in marketing, saves an offer for passengers born in the same year. This time, it’s those born in 1990, who turn 35 in 2025: she wants their list, with their date of birth.
textes.les passagers nés en 1990, du 1er janvie: the passengers born in 1990, from January 1 to December 31
textes.Il faut garder toute l’année 1990, du pr: You need to keep the whole year 1990, from the first to the last day. You can extract the year from each date, or frame the date between two bounds.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells tickets on the flights of six partner airlines, each at its own price. Odile, the sales director, already knows the most expensive ticket. Now she wants to see the 3 tickets that come right after it, from most to least expensive, to know whether they come close.
textes.seulement les 3 réservations qui suivent: only the 3 bookings that follow the most expensive one: rows 2 to 4 of the sort
textes.Range les billets du plus cher au moins: Sort the tickets from most to least expensive. Then you need to skip the first, and keep the next three.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines, from June 10 to 13, 2025. Each flight has a status: scheduled, on time, delayed, cancelled or landed. Gilles, who runs the operations center, is preparing his meeting with the airlines. He wants to know how many flights are in each status, to present a review of the period.
textes.le statut du vol (une ligne par statut): the flight status (one row per status)
textes.le nombre de vols dans ce statut: the number of flights in this status
textes.par nombre de vols, du plus grand au plu: by number of flights, largest first, then by status
textes.Il faut une ligne par statut : rassemble: You need one row per status: group the flights that share the same one, then count those in each group.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website, and each one gives their nationality. Some nationalities have only one or two people signed up, others many more. Lina, who runs the information desks, wants her signs translated first into the languages of the best-represented nationalities: those with at least 3 registered passengers.
textes.seulement les nationalités qui comptent: only the nationalities with at least 3 passengers
textes.Compte d’abord les passagers de chaque n: First count the passengers of each nationality. The threshold of 3 applies to that count: it can only be checked once the counting is done, not passenger by passenger.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the aircraft of six partner airlines, and the number of seats on each aircraft is recorded. Édouard, the airport director, is preparing a presentation brochure. He wants to highlight the size of the fleet: the total number of seats on all the partner airlines’ aircraft, as a single figure.
textes.le nombre total de sièges : la somme des: the total number of seats: the sum of the aircraft capacities
textes.Additionne les sièges de tous les avions: Add up the seats of all the aircraft: the result is a single number. There’s nothing to filter or group.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle suit: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport tracks each bag with a status: checked in, carry-on (kept by the passenger), delivered, delayed or lost. Rachid, who runs the baggage service, is reviewing the suitcases he tracks. He wants to know how many arrive safely and how many cause problems, with the number of bags in each status.
textes.le statut du bagage (une ligne par statu: the bag status (one row per status)
textes.le nombre de bagages dans ce statut: the number of bags in this status
textes.par nombre de bagages, du plus grand au: by number of bags, largest first, then by status
textes.Il faut une ligne par statut : rassemble: You need one row per status: group the bags that share the same one, then count those in each group. Count the bags themselves: a bag without a weight counts too.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells tickets on the flights of six partner airlines. Each ticket is stored with the flight booked, and some flights don’t have any yet. Every morning, at the operations center, Gilles reviews sales. He wants to see at a glance which flights are filling up and which stay empty, with their number of bookings; a flight without a ticket must appear with 0.
textes.tous les vols, y compris ceux sans réser: every flight, including those without a booking
textes.par nombre de réservations, du plus gran: by number of bookings, largest first, then by flight number
textes.Pars de tous les vols, même ceux sans bi: Start from every flight, even those without a ticket, then count their tickets. Careful: counting the rows would give 1 to an empty flight. Count the tickets actually found instead.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines. Each flight belongs to an airline, and each ticket sold on a flight has its price. For her annual review, Odile, the sales director, wants to compare what each airline took in from the tickets sold on its flights, whatever the flight’s date and status, before renegotiating their contracts.
textes.son chiffre d’affaires : la somme des pr: its revenue: the sum of the booking prices on its flights, in euros
textes.les compagnies qui ont au moins une rése: the airlines that have at least one booking
textes.Tous les billets comptent, quels que soi: Every ticket counts, whatever the flight’s date and status.
textes.Le chemin va de la compagnie à ses vols,: The path goes from the airline to its flights, then from the flights to their tickets. Then add up the ticket prices, airline by airline.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles flights that each arrive in a city; several flights sometimes serve the same city. Each ticket is stored with the flight booked. The airport is preparing a poster campaign in its hall: Coralie, in marketing, wants to feature the 5 arrival cities that attract the most bookings, all flights to each city combined.
textes.son nombre de réservations, tous vols ve: its number of bookings, all flights to this city combined
textes.seulement les 5 villes qui ont le plus d: only the 5 cities with the most bookings
textes.par nombre de réservations, du plus gran: by number of bookings, largest first, then by city
textes.Relie chaque billet à son vol, puis le v: Link each ticket to its flight, then the flight to its arrival airport to know the city. Count the tickets city by city, not flight by flight, then keep only the first five cities.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells its tickets in three classes, and each class has its usual price level. Odile, the sales director, suspects data entry errors on some Economy class tickets, sold far too expensive. She wants to reread one by one those whose price is above the average price of Economy tickets, with their flight number.
textes.seulement ceux dont le prix dépasse stri: only those whose price is strictly above the average price of “Economy” tickets
textes.Ce prix moyen se calcule sur tous les bi: This average price is calculated over all the “Economy” tickets, all flights combined.
textes.Il te faut d’abord une seule valeur : le: First you need a single value: the average price of Economy tickets, all flights combined. Then compare the price of each Economy ticket with that average, calculated separately.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets the same passenger book several tickets, on one or more flights; two tickets on the same flight make only one flight. Yannick, who runs the loyalty club, is creating a “Frequent Traveler” card. He wants to give it to the passengers who booked at least 2 different flights.
textes.son nombre de vols différents réservés: their number of different flights booked
textes.seulement les passagers qui ont réservé: only the passengers who booked at least 2 different flights
textes.par nombre de vols différents, du plus g: by number of different flights, largest first, then by last name, then by first name
textes.Deux billets sur le même vol ne comptent: Two tickets on the same flight only count as one flight.
textes.Pour chaque passager, compte ses vols di: For each passenger, count their different flights, without counting the same flight twice. The threshold of 2 applies to that count, once it’s done.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle ratta: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport links each bag, checked or carry-on, to its owner’s ticket. A passenger can have tickets without any bags. Coralie, in marketing, is launching a “travel light” offer. She wants to offer it first to the passengers who already travel without bags: those who have at least one ticket, but no bag, not even carry-on, on any of their tickets.
textes.les passagers qui ont au moins une réser: the passengers who have at least one booking
textes.seulement ceux qui n’ont aucun bagage, m: only those who have no bag, not even carry-on, on any of their bookings
textes.Pose deux questions sur chaque passager: Ask two questions about each passenger: do they have at least one ticket? Is there a bag linked to one of their tickets? Keep those who answer yes to the first and no to the second.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles the flights of six partner airlines; some haven’t sold a single ticket. At the operations center, Gilles calls these flights the “ghost flights”. Before deciding their fate with the airlines, he wants a sheet on each one, even if it’s cancelled: the airline that operates it, the city where it arrives and its status.
textes.par date de départ du vol, puis par numé: by flight departure date, then by flight number
textes.Pars de tous les vols, ajoute leur compa: Start from every flight, add their airline and their arrival airport, then look for their tickets while also keeping the flights that have none. Keep only those.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets a passenger buy several tickets, each at its own price. Yannick, who runs the loyalty club, wants to give access to the airport lounge to his best customers: those who spent more than €500 on tickets, all bookings combined.
textes.son total dépensé : la somme des prix de: their total spent: the sum of their booking prices, in euros
textes.seulement les passagers dont le total dé: only the passengers whose total spent is strictly above €500
textes.Calcule d’abord le total dépensé par cha: First calculate the total spent by each passenger. The €500 threshold applies to that total: it can only be checked once the sum is done.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle voit: At Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport, each flight is operated by an aircraft with a fixed number of seats. A flight’s fill rate compares its tickets sold with its seats: 100 × the number of tickets ÷ the number of seats. Gilles, who runs the operations center, wants to add boarding staff to the flights that fill up best: those whose rate is above 3%.
textes.la capacité de son avion : son nombre to: the capacity of its aircraft: its total number of seats
textes.son taux de remplissage, en pourcentage,: its fill rate, as a percentage out of 100, rounded to one decimal place: 100 × its number of bookings ÷ the capacity
textes.les vols dont le taux de remplissage, av: the flights whose fill rate, before rounding, is strictly above 3%
textes.par taux de remplissage arrondi, du plus: by rounded fill rate, largest first, then by flight number
textes.Compte les billets de chaque vol et divi: Count the tickets of each flight and divide by its aircraft’s capacity. A division between whole numbers loses the decimals: bring a decimal number into the calculation. The threshold applies to that rate, calculated for each flight.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines. Each one flies into one or more airports, in Europe or farther away, and several flights can arrive at the same place. Édouard, the airport director, is going to offer new flight slots. First he wants to compare the reach of their networks: the number of different arrival airports of each airline, for those that serve at least 3.
textes.son nombre d’aéroports d’arrivée différe: its number of different arrival airports, all flights combined
textes.seulement les compagnies qui desservent: only the airlines that serve at least 3 different arrival airports
textes.par nombre d’aéroports d’arrivée, du plu: by number of arrival airports, largest first, then by airline name
textes.Un aéroport desservi par plusieurs vols: An airport served by several of the airline’s flights only counts once.
textes.Pour chaque compagnie, compte ses aéropo: For each airline, count its different arrival airports, without counting the same one twice. The threshold of 3 applies to that count, once it’s done.
textes.Les passagers qui voyagent dans plusieur: The passengers who travel in several classes
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells its tickets in three classes: Economy, Premium or Business. The same passenger can travel in Economy one day, in Premium or Business the next: each ticket is sold in its own class. Odile, the sales director, wants to offer targeted upgrades to these travelers who switch classes. She’s looking for those who booked in at least 2 different classes.
textes.son nombre de classes différentes réserv: their number of different classes booked
textes.seulement les passagers qui ont réservé: only the passengers who booked in at least 2 different classes
textes.par nombre de classes différentes, du pl: by number of different classes, largest first, then by last name, then by first name
textes.Pour chaque passager, compte ses classes: For each passenger, count their different classes, without counting the same one twice. The threshold of 2 applies to that count, once it’s done.
textes.Le prix des billets selon le mois et la: Ticket prices by month and class
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle garde: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport keeps, for each ticket, its purchase date, written year-month-day, its class and its price. The month that matters here is the month the ticket was bought, not the month of the flight. Édouard, the airport director, is preparing a monthly sales review. Purchase month by purchase month, and class by class, he wants to see how many tickets are sold and at what average price.
textes.le mois de réservation, au format AAAA-M: the booking month, in YYYY-MM format, for example “2025-05” (one row per month and per class)
textes.le nombre de billets vendus ce mois-là d: the number of tickets sold that month in this class
textes.leur prix moyen, arrondi à l’euro près: their average price, rounded to the nearest euro
textes.Le mois est celui de l’achat du billet (: The month is the one when the ticket was bought (its booking date), not the month of the flight.
textes.Tire de chaque date d’achat son année et: Pull the year and month out of each purchase date. Then you need one row per month and class pair: count the tickets of each pair and take the average of their prices, rounded to the euro.
textes.Les vols qui réunissent plusieurs nation: The flights that bring together several nationalities
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport welcomes passengers from many countries; each one gave their nationality when signing up. On the same flight, the passengers sometimes have very varied nationalities. Sabrina, who runs customer service, helps the partner airlines prepare announcements in several languages. She wants to spot the most cosmopolitan flights: those whose passengers have at least 3 different nationalities.
textes.le nombre de nationalités différentes pa: the number of different nationalities among its passengers
textes.seulement les vols dont les passagers on: only the flights whose passengers have at least 3 different nationalities
textes.par nombre de nationalités, du plus gran: by number of nationalities, largest first, then by number of bookings, largest first, then by flight number
textes.Pars des vols et passe par leurs billets: Start from the flights and go through their tickets to reach the passengers and their nationality. For each flight, count the different nationalities, without duplicates; the threshold of 3 applies to that count.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines, which sell their tickets in Economy, Premium or Business class. Odile, the sales director, is helping them rethink their cabin layouts. Airline by airline, she wants to count the tickets sold in each class, each class in its own column.
textes.son nombre de billets en classe « Économ: its number of tickets in “Economy” class
textes.son nombre de billets en classe « Premiu: its number of tickets in “Premium” class
textes.son nombre de billets en classe « Affair: its number of tickets in “Business” class
textes.par nombre de billets « Économique », du: by number of “Economy” tickets, largest first, then by airline name
textes.Une ligne par compagnie, mais trois comp: One row per airline, but three counts side by side. For each column, count 1 when the ticket is in the right class and 0 otherwise, then add up.
textes.Les compagnies qui transportent le plus: The airlines that carry the most passengers
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines. Each ticket puts a passenger on an airline’s flight, and the same traveler can book several, on the same airline or not. For his annual report, Édouard, the airport director, wants to compare each airline’s customer base: how many different travelers booked at least one ticket on its flights.
textes.son nombre de passagers différents : cha: its number of different passengers: each one counts only once, even with several bookings on its flights
textes.par nombre de passagers différents, du p: by number of different passengers, largest first, then by airline name
textes.Pour chaque compagnie, passe par ses vol: For each airline, go through its flights to reach its tickets. Then count the different passengers: a regular of the airline must only count once.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle accue: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport handles flights that each arrive in a city, in Europe or farther away; each ticket sold counts for its flight’s arrival city. For the cover of the airport magazine, Coralie, in marketing, wants to draw up the ranking of arrival cities, from the most to the least in demand, with their rank based on their number of bookings.
textes.son rang : 1 pour la ville qui a le plus: its rank: 1 for the city with the most bookings, ties share the same rank and the next rank skips (1, 1, 3)
textes.les villes d’arrivée qui ont au moins un: the arrival cities that have at least one booking
textes.Compte d’abord les billets ville par vil: First count the tickets city by city. Then give each city a rank based on that count: two tied cities share the same rank, and the next rank skips a place.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle perme: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport lets travelers sign up on its website, then buy tickets. Some people signed up haven’t bought anything yet: they count as €0 in the average. Yannick, who runs the loyalty club, wants to know which travelers spend more than the average of everyone signed up, and by how much: he’ll offer them a tailored deal.
textes.son écart à la moyenne : son total moins: their gap from the average: their total minus the average of the totals, rounded to two decimal places
textes.seulement les passagers dont le total dé: only the passengers whose total is strictly above the average of the totals
textes.La moyenne des totaux porte sur tous les: The average of the totals covers every registered passenger: those without a booking count as €0.
textes.Compare chaque total à la moyenne exacte: Compare each total with the exact average, before rounding.
textes.Calcule le total de chaque passager, en: Calculate each passenger’s total, keeping those who bought nothing at €0. Then take the average of these totals, a single value, and compare each passenger with it.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle voit: At Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport, each flight is operated by an aircraft with a fixed number of seats, and not every flight fills up. A flight’s fill rate is 100 × its tickets sold ÷ its seats. At the operations center, Gilles wants the full table of flight fill rates, including those that sold no tickets: he’s looking for those for which a smaller aircraft would do.
textes.Deux vols au même taux arrondi sont à ég: Two flights with the same rounded rate are tied, even if their exact rates differ.
textes.Pars de tous les vols avec leur avion, e: Start from every flight with its aircraft, and also keep those that have no ticket. A division between whole numbers loses the decimals: bring a decimal number into the calculation. Then sort the flights on the rounded rate.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines; AlphaJet is the French airline. Each flight brings in the price of the tickets sold on it, and some flights sold nothing. AlphaJet is reviewing its fares: its sales director asks Odile, the airport’s sales director, to rank all its flights from June 10 to 13 by what they brought in, even those that sold nothing, at €0.
textes.son chiffre d’affaires : la somme des pr: its revenue: the sum of its booking prices, in euros, 0 if it has none
textes.tous les vols de la compagnie « AlphaJet: every flight of the airline “AlphaJet”, including those without a booking
textes.par rang, puis par numéro de vol: by rank, then by flight number
textes.Ne garde que les vols d’AlphaJet, et gar: Keep only AlphaJet’s flights, and also keep those that have no ticket: their empty total becomes 0. Then give each flight a rank based on that total, with ties sharing the same rank.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle garde: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport keeps, for each ticket, its purchase date and its price. Oliver Smith, a loyal traveler, has a meeting with Sabrina, who runs customer service. Before seeing him, she wants to see how the prices he paid changed, from one purchase to the next: each ticket numbered in order, with the price of the previous ticket and the difference between the two.
textes.le numéro d’ordre de la réservation : 1: the booking’s order number: 1 for the oldest, then 2, 3… with no ties
textes.le prix de la réservation précédente, ca: the price of the previous booking, an empty cell (NULL) for the first one
textes.la différence : le prix moins le prix pr: the difference: the price minus the previous price, an empty cell (NULL) for the first one
textes.seulement les réservations du passager O: only the bookings of the passenger Oliver Smith
textes.Les réservations d’Oliver Smith sont num: Oliver Smith’s bookings are numbered by booking date, then by ID; the previous one is the one that comes just before in that order.
textes.Ne garde que les billets d’Oliver Smith,: Keep only Oliver Smith’s tickets, sorted by purchase date. You need to number these purchases in order, and read on each row the price from the row before: some functions can do both without grouping the rows.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines. A ticket doesn’t say its airline: the flight booked gives it. The same traveler can take the flights of several airlines. Yannick, who runs the loyalty club, is preparing a program shared by these airlines. He’s looking for the travelers who booked with at least 2 of them, with their number of different flights.
textes.son nombre de compagnies différentes : c: their number of different airlines: those that operate the flights they booked
textes.seulement les passagers qui ont réservé: only the passengers who booked with at least 2 different airlines
textes.par nombre de compagnies, du plus grand: by number of airlines, largest first, then by number of flights, largest first, then by last name, then by first name
textes.La compagnie d’un billet se lit dans son: A ticket’s airline is read from its flight. For each passenger, count the different airlines and the different flights, without duplicates; the threshold of 2 applies to the airlines.
textes.Les vols au-dessus de la moyenne de leur: The flights above their airline’s average
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines, whose flights sell more or less well; some have no tickets. Odile, the sales director, helps each airline understand its successes. She’s looking for the flights that sell better than the average of their airline’s flights, counting flights without tickets as 0 in that average.
textes.la moyenne de réservations par vol de sa: its airline’s average number of bookings per flight, rounded to two decimal places
textes.seulement les vols dont le nombre de rés: only the flights whose number of bookings is strictly above their airline’s average
textes.par nom de la compagnie, puis par nombre: by airline name, then by number of bookings, largest first, then by flight number
textes.La moyenne d’une compagnie porte sur tou: An airline’s average covers all its flights, including those without a booking, counted as 0.
textes.Compare le nombre de réservations à la m: Compare the number of bookings with the exact average, before rounding.
textes.Deux étapes : le nombre de billets de ch: Two steps: the number of tickets of each flight, keeping empty flights at 0, then the average of these numbers for each airline. Link each flight to its own airline’s average to compare.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle trava: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport works with six partner airlines, which sell their tickets in three classes (Economy, Premium and Business). These classes don’t bring in the same amount. Odile, the sales director, wants to know which class brings in the most in each airline: the airlines will use it to adjust the number of seats in each cabin.
textes.le nom de la compagnie (une ligne par co: the airline’s name (one row per airline and per class)
textes.son chiffre d’affaires dans la compagnie: its revenue in the airline: the sum of its ticket prices, in euros
textes.le rang de la classe dans sa compagnie :: the class’s rank in its airline: 1 for the highest revenue, ties share the same rank and the next rank skips (1, 1, 3)
textes.les classes qui ont au moins une réserva: the classes that have at least one booking in the airline
textes.par nom de la compagnie, puis par rang,: by airline name, then by rank, then by class
textes.Le classement repart à 1 pour chaque com: The ranking starts again at 1 for each airline.
textes.Additionne les prix des billets pour cha: Add up the ticket prices for each airline and class pair. The rank is then given within each airline: it starts again from 1 for each one.
textes.L’aéroport Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle vend: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport sells its tickets on a website, and one click too many can create a duplicate booking: two tickets for the same passenger on the same flight. Thierry, in quality control, hunts down these duplicates. He’s looking for the passengers booked several times on the same flight, with each one’s number of tickets.
textes.le nombre de réservations de ce passager: the number of bookings of this passenger on this flight
textes.seulement les couples passager-vol qui c: only the passenger-flight pairs with at least 2 bookings
textes.par nombre de réservations, du plus gran: by number of bookings, largest first, then by last name, then by first name, then by flight number
textes.Il faut former des couples passager et v: You need to form passenger and flight pairs, then count the tickets of each pair. Keep only the pairs that have more than one.
